events.text: I want to start a taco food truck
Finding the first contact a pro would call…
Hey, I'm Carlos. I've run tacos out of a truck for twelve years. 'Taco truck' can mean a lot of things, from weekend festivals to a full daily route. Where are you right now with this?
Ready to buy a truck
I want to start a taco food truck (ready to buy a truck)
Got it. For that I'm bringing in 4 Pros. Menu drives the build, build drives permits, then we brand it and pencil the numbers.
Hi, I'm Marisol, your taco chef & menu developer. Owns menu design, recipes, and food cost margins
Hi, I'm Diego, your food truck fabricator. Owns truck build-out, equipment layout, and health code compliance
Hi, I'm Yolanda, your mobile food permit specialist. Owns licensing, commissary agreements, and health inspections
Hi, I'm Priya, your small business finance advisor. Owns startup capital, cash flow, and break-even math
Which taco tradition anchors your menu?
Birria
For a birria program, prep load matters. How many menu items feel right at launch?
3-4 tight
What's your realistic truck budget?
Actually, I also want to cater office lunches on weekdays.
Carlos is working out the change order…
Launch a birria taco truck with weekday office lunch catering.
Nice pivot—office catering changes order flow and pricing. I'm bringing in a catering sales pro to lock down corporate accounts and pre-order logistics alongside the truck.
Hi, I'm Renee, your corporate catering sales lead. Owns office catering sales, packaging, and delivery logistics
To cook birria right, we need specific gear. Which cooking equipment is non-negotiable?
Flat-top plancha, Trompo/vertical spit
How will office lunches be served?
Mix of all three
Which office types are you targeting?
Tech startups, Coworking spaces, Law/finance firms
Where will you primarily operate?
Events/festivals
How are you funding this?
Personal savings
With a $30-60k build, break-even timing shifts. What monthly take-home do you need?
Reinvesting everything
That's everything we need up front. Give us a moment while your Staff writes up your plan.
Your Staff is writing your plan…
Want me to put your Staff to work? Each Pro gets their rules, their watch list and a first assignment.
Yes, put them to work
Setting up your Staff…

chef: Lock birria recipe with chuck roast and consomé, 36-hour marinade standard. Build 3 items: quesabirria, regular taco, mulita.

truck_builder: At $30-60k budget, used step van with NSF-certified build fits; new builds run $75k+. Verify NSF trail before wiring money.
Trompo plus plancha pulls serious amperage; spec a 7-8kW diesel generator minimum, not the common 3.5kW units.
Confirm propane layout meets NFPA 58 and local fire marshal rules before fabrication starts.
catering: Build a 50-contact outreach list across tech, coworking, and law firms before truck delivery. Cold email open rates run 20-30 percent.
Offer three serve styles: truck pull-up, drop-off trays, and build-your-own bar. Price drop-off at $18-22 per head.
Include one vegetarian option like mushroom or jackfruit birria; law and finance firms ask about it most.
permits: Events and festivals still require a commissary contract in most cities, typically $400-900 monthly. Line this up before truck purchase.
Depends on your city, but most require mobile food vendor permit, health permit, and seller's permit. Budget 4-8 weeks for approvals.
Get fire suppression (Ansul) inspected and tagged; festival organizers will ask for the certificate.
finance: Hold 3 months of fixed costs in reserve, roughly $8-12k covering commissary, insurance, fuel, and propane before opening.
Reinvesting everything is fine short-term, but pay yourself $500 weekly by month 4 to avoid burnout decisions.
Track food cost under 32 percent and labor under 25 percent; birria meat yield after braising runs about 55 percent.

catering.title: 50-Office Prospect List: Weekday Lunch Catering Targets
catering.summary: Framework and sample prospect list structure to identify 50 offices for birria catering outreach, since specific companies depend on your city.
catering.body:
## How to Use This List

Since I don't know your operating city, I've built this as a **targeting framework** plus columns to fill. Pull names from LinkedIn Sales Navigator, local Business Journal "Best Places to Work," coworking directories (WeWork, Industrious, Regus), and your Chamber of Commerce.

## Ideal Prospect Profile

- **Headcount:** 25–150 employees (sweet spot for 1-truck catering)
- **Lunch budget signals:** catered Friday lunches, free snacks, Zerocater/EzCater users
- **Location:** within 15 min of your commissary/park spot

## Target Mix (aim for ~50)

| Segment | Target Count | Why They Buy |
|---|---|---|
| Tech startups (Series A–C) | 20 | Perk culture, recurring Friday lunches |
| Coworking spaces | 10 | Member events, tenant appreciation days |
| Law firms (mid-size) | 10 | Client lunches, long-hours associate meals |
| Finance/wealth management | 10 | Client entertainment, quarterly team lunches |

## Columns to Build in Your Sheet

- Company name
- Office address + # of employees
- Office/EA/People Ops contact (name, email, LinkedIn)
- Current catering vendor (if visible)
- Likely weekly budget — **typically $12–20/head** in most US markets, higher in NYC/SF
- Preferred service style (truck pull-up, drop-off, individual boxes)
- Last touch date + next action

## Quick Sourcing Tips

- Search LinkedIn: "Office Manager" + your city
- Walk coworking lobbies — ask for the community manager
- Offer a **free 10-person tasting** to anchor the first 5 accounts

— Renee

truck_builder.title: Three-Truck Comparison Sheet: Birria Build Options
truck_builder.summary: Side-by-side look at three realistic truck paths for your birria + plancha + trompo program at $30-60k.
truck_builder.body:
## Three-Truck Comparison for a Birria + Trompo Build

All prices are **typical ranges** — final cost depends on your city's permitting, inspector, and local upfitter. Verify with 2-3 local fabricators before committing.

| Factor | A) Used Step Van Rebuild | B) Mid-Grade Turnkey Used Truck | C) New Concession Trailer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Typical all-in cost** | $28-45k | $45-60k | $35-55k |
| **Base vehicle** | 14-18ft used step van | 16-22ft used food truck | Pull-behind trailer (needs tow vehicle) |
| **Fits plancha + trompo?** | Tight — custom layout required | Usually yes, may need swap-outs | Yes, easiest to design around |
| **Festival/event friendly** | Strong — self-propelled | Strongest — plug and go | Depends on event tow/parking rules |
| **Office lot access** | Good | Good | Harder — tow + unhook time |
| **Timeline to serve** | 10-16 weeks | 2-6 weeks | 8-14 weeks |
| **Hidden risk** | Engine/transmission on old chassis | Prior owner's shortcuts, hood/suppression age | Need reliable tow vehicle + storage |

## My Recommendation for Your Mix

- **Festivals-first + reinvesting everything** → Option **B** gets you earning fastest, which matters when you're self-funding.
- Confirm the **Ansul hood** covers both plancha and trompo flame load — this is the single most common failure point on resale trucks.
- Budget **$3-5k reserve** outside the build for health dept., commissary deposit, and first fire inspection re-visit.

– Diego

chef.title: Three-Item Birria Menu Spec
chef.summary: A tight launch menu built for plancha + trompo workflow, event lines, and office catering repeatability.
chef.body:
## Core Philosophy
Three items, one braise, one trompo cut. Everything shares the consommé and adobo so prep stays sane and food cost drops.

## The Three Items

| Item | Build | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Quesabirria** | Plancha-dipped tortilla, Oaxaca cheese, shredded birria, onion/cilantro, consommé cup | Hero item, 55-65% of mix |
| **Birria Trompo Taco** | Marinated beef (or beef/lamb blend) shaved off vertical spit onto fresh corn tortilla, salsa verde cruda | Visual theater, premium price |
| **Mulita** | Two plancha tortillas, double cheese, birria, grilled onion | Catering workhorse — holds 20+ min in warmer |

## Why This Trio Works for You
- **Shared mise:** one adobo (guajillo, ancho, chile de árbol, tomato, garlic, cumin, clove, cinnamon) feeds all three.
- **Plancha + trompo both earn their keep** — the trompo is your festival magnet; plancha handles catering volume.
- **Office catering fit:** quesabirria and mulitas travel well in insulated pans; consommé goes in 4oz portion cups.

## Pricing Guardrails (verify locally)
Typical urban truck pricing runs roughly **$5–7 quesabirria, $4–5 trompo taco, $7–9 mulita**, with consommé **$2–3**. Your city's beef chuck/shank cost and permit load will shift this — price-test at your first three events before locking a catering sheet.

## Next Steps
- Lock adobo recipe over 2 test batches
- Decide beef-only vs. beef/lamb trompo (lamb raises cost ~20–35%)
- Build a per-item cost card once your meat vendor is chosen

— Marisol

permits.title: Permit and Commissary Checklist — Birria Taco Truck Launch
permits.summary: A sequenced checklist of permits, inspections, and commissary setup you need before serving your first birria taco.
permits.body:
## 1. Business Foundation
- **Form LLC** with your state (typical filing: $50–$500)
- **EIN** from IRS (free, same day online)
- **Business license** from your city (typical: $50–$400/year)
- **Sales tax permit** from state revenue dept
- **DBA filing** if operating under a trade name

## 2. Food Safety Certifications
- **Food Handler Card** for every employee (varies by state; often $10–$25)
- **Food Protection Manager** (ServSafe or equivalent) — usually required for the owner/operator
- **Allergen training** — required in some states; confirm with your local health dept

## 3. Mobile Food Vendor Permits
- **Mobile Food Facility (MFF) permit** from county health dept (ranges widely, often $400–$1,500/year)
- **Truck plan review** before build-out — submit layout, equipment specs, plumbing
- **Fire marshal inspection** — critical for your **trompo/vertical spit** (propane use triggers extra scrutiny)
- **Health inspection** post-build before first service
- **Event/festival vendor permits** — many festivals require separate temporary event permits

## 4. Commissary Kitchen (Legally Required in Most Jurisdictions)
| Need | Why |
|---|---|
| Signed commissary agreement | Required by health dept for permit approval |
| Overnight truck parking | Many codes prohibit storing trucks at home |
| Prep space for birria braise | Long-cook consomé is easier off-truck |
| Potable water fill / graywater disposal | Daily servicing required |

- Typical commissary cost: **$400–$1,200/month**
- Confirm it's **health-dept approved** in your jurisdiction

## 5. Insurance
- **General liability** ($1M typical minimum for events)
- **Commercial auto** on the truck
- **Workers' comp** once you hire

## 6. Before First Service
- Weights & Measures seal on any scales
- Propane tank certification
- Final health inspection sign-off
- Festival-specific COI with organizer named as additional insured

*Permit names, fees, and sequence vary by city and county — verify every item with your local health department before paying.*

finance.title: Startup Budget and Break-Even Model: Birria Truck Launch
finance.summary: A realistic cost build and sales-per-day target so you know what the truck must do to sustain itself.
finance.body:
## Startup Costs (Typical Ranges)

| Category | Low | High | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Used truck + build-out (plancha + trompo) | $30,000 | $60,000 | Trompo adds $1.5–3k; verify hood/fire suppression |
| Permits, LLC, health cert, commissary | $1,500 | $5,000 | Varies heavily by city/state |
| Insurance (annual, paid upfront) | $2,500 | $5,000 | GL + auto + workers' comp if hiring |
| Smallwares, pans, consomé cups | $1,500 | $3,000 | |
| POS, Square/Toast hardware | $500 | $1,500 | |
| Initial inventory (chuck, chilies, tortillas) | $1,500 | $3,000 | |
| Branding, wrap, website | $2,000 | $6,000 | |
| **Working capital buffer (2 mo)** | $8,000 | $12,000 | Non-negotiable |
| **Total** | **~$47k** | **~$95k** | |

Savings-funded means **cap total at the low end** and keep that buffer intact.

## Break-Even Math (Monthly)

- Fixed costs: commissary, insurance, permits, phone, software ≈ **$2,000–3,500/mo**
- Variable: food + packaging ≈ **30–35%** of revenue
- Fuel/propane: **$400–800/mo**

**Break-even revenue ≈ $4,500–6,500/mo**, roughly **$225–325/day** over 20 service days.

## What That Looks Like

- At a **$14 avg ticket**, break-even = **16–23 tacos/plates per day**
- Festival days should clear **$1,500–3,000** gross — these fund slow weeks
- Office catering trays at **$180–280 each** — two bookings/week covers fixed costs alone

Since you're reinvesting everything, treat months 1–6 as **data collection**: track food cost %, labor hours, and catering-vs-event margin weekly.

**Next:** confirm your city's commissary and permit fees before locking the truck purchase.

[Your name]

lead.text: Carlos, what should I focus on this week? Keep it short.

This week, lock in two things:

1. **Open the business bank account** with your EIN and move your savings in — nothing else can move until money has a home.
2. **Call the three commissaries Yolanda shortlists and tour one.** Everything (permits, prep, insurance) hinges on having a commissary address.

If you have time left, skim Yolanda's commissary contract checklist before your tour so you walk in knowing what to ask.

finance.text: Priya, quick one: with $7 tacos and two $350 catering gigs a week, about how many tacos a day do I need to break even? Two or three sentences.

With $3,600/month in fixed costs and catering throwing off ~$2,170/month in gross profit, you only need to clear about **$1,430 from truck tacos** — roughly **13 tacos/day** across 22 operating days. Without the catering, that jumps to ~33/day. Catering is quietly carrying the model, so protecting those 2 gigs/week matters a lot.

chatNote: Real chats with the Lead and Priya through their own Claude Code sessions (2026-11-01).
